newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Yen rally squeezes NZ dollar TWI, MCI below -1.00.
newsitem.headline: Yen rally squeezes NZ dollar TWI, MCI below -1.00.

text.p: Sharp gains by the Japanese yen over the U.S. dollar in late morning Tokyo took the New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index down nearly 30 points to below 67.20 on Monday.
The yen's strength knocked on to the Monetary Conditions Index (MCI), which showed market conditions about 100 basis points easier than the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's official desired level.
Forex dealers said the moves in the TWI were entirely dollar/yen driven and bore little relation to the kiwi dollar.
Meanwhile, short bank bill rates moved upwards but failed to cancel out the impact of the falling TWI on the MCI.
The TWI had started Monday's session at 67.47 and the MCI at -0.90. Shortly before 3.30 p.m. (0330 GMT) the MCI dropped to -1.03 as the TWI dipped to 67.18.
At the same time the 90-day bill rate was at 7.11 percent, up 10 basis points from its open.
The MCI is based on conditions around a base line derived from a 90-day bill rate of 7.5 percent and a TWI at 68.00.

Although a number of money market observers told Reuters late last week they felt the RBNZ was likely to express its concern at the easing in conditions, the yen-driven TWI shift during Monday appeared beyond the bank's reach, dealers said.
"The RB is caught between a rock and a hard place," ANZ Investment Bank's Murray Hindley said.

The most likely escape route would be a rebound in the dollar/yen from the sub-112 levels seen during Monday, he added. Dealers said the expectation from Tokyo and other major centres was that the dollar would bounce back in the fairly near term.
